answer: The walnut graph is rebuilt each epoch, and therefore the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the mirror audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 8 times its size, so a group of 52 keys loses far more than 52 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the karst checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 38 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
